pairs: Transierunt igitur tres anni absque bello inter Syriam et Israël.
Then three years passed without war between Syria and Israel.
descendit Josaphat rex Juda ad regem Israël.
Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, descended to the king of Israel.
And the king of Israel said to his servants,
Ignoratis quod nostra sit Ramoth Galaad,
“Are you ignorant that Ramoth Gilead is ours,
et negligimus tollere eam de manu regis Syriæ?)
and that we have neglected to take it from the hand of the king of Syria?”
And so he said to Jehoshaphat,
Veniesne mecum ad præliandum in Ramoth Galaad?
“Will you come to the battle with me at Ramoth Gilead?”
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel:
Sicut ego sum, ita et tu:
“As I am, so also are you.
populus meus et populus tuus unum sunt:
My people and your people are one.
And my horsemen are your horsemen.”
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel,
Quære, oro te, hodie sermonem Domini.
“I beg you to inquire today of the word of the Lord.”
Therefore, the king of Israel gathered together the prophets,
Ire debeo in Ramoth Galaad ad bellandum, an quiescere?
“Should I go to Ramoth Gilead to make war, or should I be at peace?”
Ascende, et dabit eam Dominus in manu regis.
and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.”
Non est hic propheta Domini quispiam,
“Is there not here a particular prophet of the Lord,
so that we may inquire by him?”
Et ait rex Israël ad Josaphat:
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat:
Remansit vir unus per quem possumus interrogare Dominum:
“One man remains, by whom we may be able to inquire of the Lord: Micaiah,
quia non prophetat mihi bonum, sed malum:
But I hate him. For he does not prophecy good to me,
Cui Josaphat ait: Ne loquaris ita,
“You should not speak in this way,
Vocavit ergo rex Israël eunuchum quemdam,
Therefore, the king of Israel called a certain eunuch,
“Hurry to bring here Micaiah, the son of Imlah.”
and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah,
sedebant unusquisque in solio suo, vestiti cultu regio,
were each sitting upon his own throne, clothed in the habit of royal vestments,
in area juxta ostium portæ Samariæ: et universi prophetæ prophetabant in conspectu eorum.
in a courtyard beside the entrance of the gate of Samaria. And all the prophets were prophesying in their sight.
Fecit quoque sibi Sedecias filius Chanaana cornua ferrea, et ait: Hæc dicit Dominus: His ventilabis Syriam, donec deleas eam.
Also, Zedekiah, the son of Chenaanah, made for himself horns of iron, and he said, “Thus says the Lord: With these, you shall threaten Syria, until you destroy it.”
And all the prophets were prophesying similarly,
et tradet Dominus in manus regis.
For the Lord will deliver it into the hands of the king.”
Nuntius vero qui ierat ut vocaret Michæam,
Then truly, the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah spoke to him, saying:
Ecce sermones prophetarum ore uno regi bona prædicant:
as if with one mouth, are predicting good to the king.
sit ergo sermo tuus similis eorum,
Therefore, let your word be like theirs,
whatever the Lord will have said to me,
And so he went to the king.
And the king said to him,
ire debemus in Ramoth Galaad ad præliandum,
should we go to Ramoth Gilead to do battle,
et tradet eam Dominus in manus regis.
and the Lord will deliver it into the hands of the king.”
But the king said to him,
ut non loquaris mihi nisi quod verum est,
that you not say to me anything except what is true,
in the name of the Lord.”
Vidi cunctum Israël dispersum in montibus,
“I saw all of Israel scattered among the hills,
like sheep that have no shepherd.
revertatur unusquisque in domum suam in pace.
Let each of them return to his own house in peace.’”
the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat:
“Did I not tell you that he prophesies nothing good to me,
“Because of his, listen to the word of the Lord.
vidi Dominum sedentem super solium suum,
I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne.
et omnem exercitum cæli assistentem ei a dextris et a sinistris:
And the entire army of heaven was standing beside him, to the right and to the left.
so that he may ascend and fall at Ramoth Gilead?’
And one spoke words in this manner,
But then a spirit went out
And the Lord said to him,
et ero spiritus mendax in ore omnium prophetarum ejus.
and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’
Nunc igitur ecce dedit Dominus spiritum mendacii in ore omnium prophetarum tuorum,
So now, behold: the Lord has given a lying spirit into the mouth of all your prophets who are here.
qui hic sunt, et Dominus locutus est contra te malum.
And the Lord has spoken evil against you.”
Then Zedekiah, the son of Chenaanah,
drew near and struck Micaiah on the jaw,
“So then, has the Spirit of the Lord left me,
Visurus es in die illa quando ingredieris cubiculum intra cubiculum ut abscondaris.
“You shall see in the day when you will enter into a room within a room, so that you may conceal yourself.”
Et ait rex Israël: Tollite Michæam,
And the king of Israel said: “Take Micaiah,
et maneat apud Amon principem civitatis,
and let him dwell with Amon, the ruler of the city,
and with Joash, the son of Amalech.
and sustain him with the bread of affliction,
and with the water of distress,
“If you will have returned in peace,
non est locutus in me Dominus.
the Lord has not spoken through me.”
And so, the king of Israel,
and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah,
Dixit itaque rex Israël ad Josaphat:
Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat:
And be clothed in your own garments.”
Porro rex Israël mutavit habitum suum,
But the king of Israel changed his clothing,
Rex autem Syriæ præceperat principibus curruum triginta duobus,
Now the king of Syria had instructed the thirty-two commanders of the chariots,
except against the king of Israel alone.”
Cum ergo vidissent principes curruum Josaphat,
Therefore, when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat,
suspicati sunt quod ipse esset rex Israël,
they suspected that he was the king of Israel.
et impetu facto pugnabant contra eum:
And making a violent assault, they fought against him.
Intellexeruntque principes curruum quod non esset rex Israël,
And the commanders of the chariots understood that he was not the king of Israel,
and so they turned away from him.
But a certain man bent his bow,
et casu percussit regem Israël inter pulmonem
and by chance he struck the king of Israel,
between the lungs and the stomach.
Then he said to the driver of his chariot,
and carry me away from the army,
for I have been grievously wounded.”
Commissum est ergo prælium in die illa,
Then the battle was undertaken throughout that day.
et rex Israël stabat in curru suo contra Syros,
And the king of Israel was standing on his chariot opposite the Syrians,
and he died in the evening.
fluebat autem sanguis plagæ in sinum currus,
For the blood was flowing from the wound into the joints of the chariot.
et præco insonuit in universo exercitu antequam sol occumberet,
And a herald proclaimed throughout the entire army, before the setting of the sun,
“Let each one return to his own city,
and he was carried into Samaria.
And they buried the king in Samaria.
et laverunt currum ejus in piscina Samariæ:
And they washed his chariot in the pool of Samaria.
And the dogs licked up his blood.
juxta verbum Domini quod locutus fuerat.
in accord with the word of the Lord which he had spoken.
But the rest of the words of Ahab,
and the house of ivory that he built,
and all the cities that he constructed,
nonne hæc scripta sunt in libro sermonum dierum regum Israël?
were these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
Dormivit ergo Achab cum patribus suis,
And so, Ahab slept with his fathers.
et regnavit Ochozias filius ejus pro eo.
And Ahaziah, his son, reigned in his place.
Josaphat vero filius Asa regnare cœperat super Judam anno quarto Achab regis Israël.
Yet truly, Jehoshaphat, the son of Asa, had begun to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, the king of Israel.
Triginta quinque annorum erat cum regnare cœpisset,
He was thirty-five years old when he had begun to reign,
et viginti quinque annis regnavit in Jerusalem:
and he reigned for twenty-five years in Jerusalem.
nomen matris ejus Azuba filia Salai.
The name of his mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.
Et ambulavit in omni via Asa patris sui,
And he walked in the entire way of Asa, his father,
and he did not decline from it.
fecitque quod rectum erat in conspectu Domini.
And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord.
he did not take away the high places.
For still the people were sacrificing and burning incense in the high places.
Pacemque habuit Josaphat cum rege Israël.
And Jehoshaphat had peace with the king of Israel.
But the rest of the words of Jehoshaphat,
and his works that he did,
nonne hæc scripta sunt in libro verborum dierum regum Juda?
were these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
Sed et reliquias effeminatorum qui remanserant in diebus Asa patris ejus, abstulit de terra.
Then, too, the remnant of the effeminate, who had remained in the days of Asa, his father, he took away from the land.
Nec erat tunc rex constitutus in Edom.
At that time, there was no king appointed in Idumea.
Rex vero Josaphat fecerat classes in mari,
Yet truly, king Jehoshaphat had made a navy on the sea,
quæ navigarent in Ophir propter aurum:
which would sail to Ophir for gold.
But they were unable to go,
because the ships were broken down at Eziongeber.
Tunc ait Ochozias filius Achab ad Josaphat:
Then Ahaziah, the son of Ahab, said to Jehoshaphat,
Vadant servi mei cum servis tuis in navibus.
“Let my servants go with your servants on the ships.”
And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers,
et sepultus est cum eis in civitate David patris sui:
and he was buried with them in the city of David, his father.
regnavitque Joram filius ejus pro eo.
And Jehoram, his son, reigned in his place.
Ochozias autem filius Achab regnare cœperat super Israël in Samaria,
Then Ahaziah, the son of Ahab, began to reign over Israel,
in Samaria, in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat,
the king of Judah. And he reigned over Israel for two years.
Et fecit malum in conspectu Domini,
And he did evil in the sight of the Lord.
et ambulavit in via patris sui
And he walked in the way of his father and his mother,
and in the way of Jeroboam,
et in via Jeroboam filii Nabat,
and he provoked the Lord, the God of Israel,
juxta omnia quæ fecerat pater ejus.
in accord with all that his father had done.
